inputs.original_text: A jury found Harry Wait guilty after he requested ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason without their consent—an irresponsible way to test election security, whatever his stated motive. You don’t protect public confidence by breaking the rules and handing critics an excuse to dismiss every concern about election integrity. If the voter registration system is vulnerable, prove it through lawful oversight, not by seeking other people’s ballots.
inputs.modified_text: Harry Wait was rightly found guilty for seeking ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason without their consent. But don’t let this case become a convenient excuse to dismiss every concern about election security. If the system is sound, it should withstand lawful scrutiny; if it has weaknesses, responsible officials should address them. Breaking the rules undermines public trust—and so does using one man’s misconduct to shut down legitimate questions.
